item.title: 'A money making racket': Angry British dual nationals blast UK passport demand
item.description: With the end of the Electronic Travel Authorisation system's 'tolerance period' approaching, British readers of The Local have slammed unclear government guidance about a rule change meaning dual nationals must enter the country on a valid UK passport.

item.title: Swedish Fika Calendar: Semla, the scrumptious treat that slayed a king
item.description: The Local's Fika Calendar walks you through a whole year of Sweden's coffee-and-cake tradition, with information on the pastries and the history behind them. Today: save some space in your tummy for the indulgent, cream-filled semla.

item.title: Swedish parliament rejects joint proposal to stop teen deportations
item.description: The Swedish parliament's social insurance committee voted 'no' this afternoon on a joint proposal from the Green Party and the Left Party that was intended to reduce the number of so-called teen deportations.

item.title: Russia increasing hybrid threats around Sweden, say military intelligence
item.description: Russia has stepped up its hybrid threat activities and seems willing to take greater risks in Sweden and the region, the head of Sweden's military intelligence told AFP on Tuesday.

item.title: Swedish Migration Court denies teen deportation appeal in guiding ruling
item.description: In a key ruling on a 'teenage deportation' case, the Swedish Migration Court of Appeal has denied a Swedish residence permit to a young woman.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: grina
item.description: Here's a word with not one meaning, but two, depending on where in Sweden you are.

item.title: Parents lash out at Sweden's 'absurd' teen deportations
item.description: This week’s episode of Sweden in Focus Extra features an interview with the father of a high school student facing expulsion from Sweden, as well as analysis of the latest developments on teen deportations.

item.title: 17th century wreck reappears from Stockholm deep
item.description: A 17th century Swedish Navy shipwreck buried underwater in central Stockholm for 400 years has suddenly become visible due to unusually low Baltic Sea levels.

item.title: 'Sweden is saying it wants experienced workers, but not their kids'
item.description: Software developer Besnik Barani works at one of Sweden's biggest engineering companies, while his daughter is a paid intern at Chalmers Institute of Technology. If the appeal in her teen deportation case fails, Sweden could end up losing both of them.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Wednesday
item.description: Sharp decline in immigrant unemployment, government earmarks 70 million for return migration, joint proposal to stop teen deportations rejected and more news from Sweden on Wednesday.
